brief.objective: RESEARCH (plan-only, per the standing research-before-plan rule): COORDINATION-LAYER RELIABILITY FOR LLM AGENT FACTORIES. Context: in one session the Rizzstack coordinator produced six failure classes, each mechanically possible: (FC-1) briefs omitting commit+push so finished work sat untracked in workspaces; (FC-2) an infra restart fired into an active lane, destroying uncommitted workspace work; (FC-3) a dispatcher accepted a padded/fabricated revision id (format-valid, not resolvable) and leased work against a nonexistent commit; (FC-4) coordinator manual interventions duplicated automated machinery mid-flight; (FC-5) a changelog/coverage registry that enforces entries AFTER merge, creating a one-merge-behind chase; (FC-6) immutable per-attempt file leases that dead-end when the coordinator mis-lists paths (no amendment path; only re-dispatch). RESEARCH TASK: establish the current best practice (as of today, 2026) for preventing each class MECHANICALLY rather than procedurally - search the web for how mature autonomous-agent orchestration systems (OpenAI Codex agent harnesses, Claude Code task tooling, SWE-agent/SWE-bench harness patterns, AutoGen/CrewAI orchestrators, Google ADK, AWS Bedrock agent infra, CI/CD release automation like release-please/changesets for the registry problem, database transaction/outbox patterns for event emission) handle: work-contract enforcement at task admission, transactional workspace lifecycle (commit-before-teardown, restart fences), dispatcher input validation against real revisions (resolve-then-lease), human-vs-automation role separation (operator dashboards that prevent duplicate manual action), merge-time metadata automation (self-registering PRs), and mutable-vs-immutable capability grants. Deliver docs/coordination-reliability-research.md: per failure class - the best-practice mechanism (with citations/URLs + dates), how rizzstack's current machinery compares (name the exact files: hyvv launcher.py, bundlebees agent_consumer.py/cli.py, workflow test_docs_parity.py), and the concrete work-package decomposition (gate format AC-NNN -> proven-by path::test) that would install each mechanism. PLAN-ONLY: no implementation. COMMIT on branch docs/coordination-reliability-research before ending the turn.
